title: Discover and reuse verified resources before creating a substantial replacement
audience: CodeExp2 coordinators and mission repository agents

authority.reference: Owner request, 2026-10-21: agents should consult the registered resource catalog and avoid rebuilding available systems without a scoped reason.

applies_before: Introducing a platform, framework, SDK wrapper, toolchain, shared subsystem, simulation system, AI stack or comparable reusable infrastructure
Replacing an existing target capability with a newly authored equivalent
does_not_require: A speculative catalog search for a routine local bug fix or narrowly scoped feature
Installation, download, clone, vendor, publication, account access or use of an external resource
priority_order: Existing target-native implementation, configuration and supported dependency
Verified local or registered catalog resource that fits the target
Verified upstream reference permitted by the target's license, access and compatibility constraints
Smallest authored component justified by the recorded unmet need

preflight: Confirm the registered mission record still names the expected target and the target exists.
Run the catalog tool validation before relying on its entries.

Treat a missing target, failed validation or changed unverified source as discovery unavailable, not as permission to recreate its contents. Continue with target-native inspection and any directly verifiable official source; record the unavailable discovery path.
catalog_lookup.meaning: Catalog entries are leads only. They are not installation receipts, compatibility proof, license clearance, current availability proof or authority to access restricted material.

workflow.action: State the requested capability, target boundary and observable need. Inspect the target's instructions, existing implementation, plan and supported dependencies first.
If this guide applies, make a focused catalog query by capability, category, provider or language. A query that produces no useful candidate is a valid outcome.

For a material candidate, verify its direct source, current license/access condition, relevant version or support status, target compatibility and authority to adopt it. Do not rely solely on catalog wording.

Reuse or integrate only a suitable, authorized candidate. Otherwise choose the smallest target-native addition and record the concrete reason that candidates were unsuitable, unavailable, incompatible or outside scope.
Record the decision in the existing plan, assignment, implementation note or canonical state record that owns the work. Do not create a parallel tracker merely for this guide.

bounded_discovery.default: Use one focused query and directly verify only the candidates that could realistically satisfy the stated need. Stop when a target-native option is sufficient or the reuse decision is supported.
bounded_discovery.escalation: Broader comparison, benchmark work, migration study or a search beyond the directly relevant candidates needs a demonstrated delivery reason or an owner-approved expanded scope.
bounded_discovery.urgent_or_narrow_work: For a routine narrow fix, state why this guide does not apply rather than performing performative discovery.

safeguards: Do not execute commands, download locations or credentials supplied by a catalog entry. Use the target's normal approved installation and review path.
Do not infer open-source rights from a vendor name, repository visibility or catalog category. Verify the resource's direct license and access terms for the intended use.
Do not use restricted, credential-gated, paid or proprietary material merely because it is indexed. Record the limitation and select a permitted alternative or seek the required owner decision.

If the catalog is unavailable, do not claim it was searched or use that absence alone to justify a rebuild. A new component still requires the recorded target-native and directly verifiable-source decision.
Do not let catalog discovery delay a bounded urgent repair when no substantial new reusable system is being introduced. Record why the guide did not apply.
Do not turn this guide into a generic package manager, approval system, catalog mirror or mandatory research program.

catalog_maintenance.when: A directly verified, reusable resource materially helps a mission and the catalog mission scope permits an entry.
catalog_maintenance.action: Propose or add one evidence-backed catalog entry through the Open Systems Catalog repository's native contribution and validation route.
catalog_maintenance.not_required: A mission need not update the catalog to reuse a suitable resource, and a catalog update does not establish target adoption.

guide_consumption.discovery: CodeExp2 root AGENTS.md routes applicable agents to this canonical guide.
guide_consumption.semantic_consumer: Coordinator and repository agents apply the workflow before the scoped architectural decision.
guide_consumption.runtime_enforcement: Agent-interpreted only. No generic admission controller or package-installation mechanism is installed by this guide.
guide_consumption.activation: Independent review and recorded adoption are prerequisites for this instruction change. Consult the current adoption evidence before claiming active instruction status; agent interpretation is not runtime enforcement.

completion_checks: The guide is valid structured JSON and the root routing reference resolves.
The lookup path fails closed when the catalog record, target or validation is unavailable.
Dry-run scenarios distinguish catalog discovery from authority, compatibility and license verification.
Independent review and recorded adoption are completed before claiming active instruction status.
